title: The Fall of Proud Moab
overview: This chapter announces the destruction of Moab, Israel's neighbor east of the Dead Sea, for its pride and its mocking of Israel, mixes that judgment with deep mourning, and ends with a promise that Moab will one day be restored.

parts.label: Moab's towns fall (vv. 1-10)
parts.note: Town after town in Moab is pictured falling, and even Chemosh, Moab's national god, is carried off like captured loot. Verse 10 harshly curses any invader who holds back the sword, calling the slaughter the LORD's work, and the text does not soften this.

parts.label: Wine left on its dregs (vv. 11-13)
parts.note: Wine left sitting on its sediment kept its strong taste, and Moab, never uprooted by invasion, had stayed settled and unchanged. Now invaders will pour it out and smash its jars, and Moab will find Chemosh as useless as Israel found its golden calf shrine at Bethel.

parts.label: The boastful are broken (vv. 14-25)
parts.note: Moab's soldiers boast, but its staff and its horn, both pictures of power and rule, are broken. The long list of towns stresses that no place, near or far, is spared.

parts.label: The mocker is mocked (vv. 26-30)
parts.note: Moab is pictured staggering like a drunk, made to drink God's anger, and becomes a laughingstock because it once laughed at Israel's downfall. Its people leave their cities to hide in the cliffs like doves.

parts.label: Weeping over Moab (vv. 31-39)
parts.note: Surprisingly, the speaker weeps for Moab, mourning its famous vineyards and its silenced harvest songs. Shaved heads, cut hands and rough sackcloth were common signs of grief, and much of this passage echoes an earlier lament over Moab in Isaiah 15 and 16.

parts.label: No escape, then hope (vv. 40-47)
parts.note: An eagle, usually taken to be Babylon's army, swoops down, and anyone who escapes one danger falls into the next, while verse 45 reuses lines from an old victory song about Heshbon. Yet the final verse promises that the LORD will restore Moab's fortunes in days to come, without saying what that will look like.

think: When a proud or powerful group falls, can a person feel both that it was deserved and real grief for the people caught in it, and what does holding both feel like?
